rationale: The workflow runs on push and pull_request with a multi-configuration matrix, so repeated pushes to the same branch/PR can spawn superseded in-progress runs. fail-fast is already the GitHub Actions default (true), so explicitly setting it would be a no-op, and a custom timeout is unsafe here because observed runs vary from about 2 to 12 minutes (a tight limit risks false timeouts on valid slow runs, while a generous limit saves nothing on the observed workload). The supported, safe fit is P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: add a top-level concurrency group keyed by workflow and ref with cancel-in-progress: true. This cancels only stale in-progress runs for the same branch/PR (branches and PRs are partitioned, so distinct branches do not share a cancellation group), preserves full build/test coverage on the latest run, keeps canceled runs in the audit record, and adds no permissions, secrets, deployment, publishing, or new network access. Prerequisites are met (same workflow; newer revision supersedes older checks) and the release/deployment and shared-cancellation-group contraindications do not apply.
